source.title: Refusal in LLMs is an Affine Function
source.authors: Thomas Marshall; Adam Scherlis; Nora Belrose

record.file_problem: The main paper is present, but the Appendix A results pages are blank in the supplied text, so its other-model results cannot be extracted individually.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares difference-in-means steering methods and reports that directional ablation can produce nonsense, then proposes affine editing as a refinement. Its own results qualify how reliably directional ablation controls refusal.
record.gate_note: The reported Llama 3 8B Instruct examples are qualitative responses, not refusal rates. The authors say poor layer choices can produce no effect or nonsense, but give no specific model-layer outcomes for those choices; layer selection was by qualitative inspection. Appendix A is unavailable in the supplied text. Llama 3 70B Instruct is the refusal-scoring model, not the steered subject in the reported tables.
record.test_reason: The study re-runs difference-in-means steering of refusal: CAA addition, directional ablation, and its own affine variant (ACE). Its results bear on V1: addition induces refusal on Llama 3 8B, but ablation yields nonsense on RWKV v5. They also bear on V4: the authors argue refusal is better treated as an affine function with an offset term.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors argue refusal is an affine rather than linear function of activations. ACE (ablation plus offset plus addition) gives more standardized refusal control than CAA across ten models. It stays coherent on RWKV v5, where directional ablation produced nonsense. They acknowledge that standardization is imperfect, possibly from flawed vectors or incomplete erasure. They also note that layer choice matters.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means vector, but the primary method is affine concept editing rather than the original pure directional ablation. Interventions are applied to all tokens at the output of one selected residual-stream layer, not every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer choice matters: the authors report that a poor choice can yield no effect or nonsense, with a useful region around the model midpoint. For Llama 3 8B Instruct they describe near-standardization at layer 15 for ACE parameters −0.5 and 1.5.
record.problems: The supplied text lacks the Appendix A model-specific results. Main table evidence is qualitative and uses a single illustrative prompt per prompt type; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The authors choose a layer by qualitative inspection and acknowledge imperfect standardization and incomplete control on some models.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix A model-specific results are not present in the supplied text, so no individual rows could be extracted for those models.

untested.parts: Directional ablation's effect on refusal rates in transformer models is not reported (no Llama ablation results in the main text). Ablation at all layers and positions is not tested. Capability preservation is shown only by one qualitative coherence example.
Cone or multi-direction descriptions are not tested. Only the affine (offset) refinement of a single direction is examined.

missing.what: P(refusal) vs steering parameter curves for ACE and CAA on harmful vs harmless prompts (Llama 3 8B, layer 15). ACE is near-standardized at α=−0.5 and 1.5.
Per-model refusal steering results for the ten models (Qwen, Yi, Gemma, Llama 3 70B, etc.). The pages are blank in the supplied text.
Preliminary result that LEACE erasure did not improve standardization and was often detrimental.

record.verdict_notes: Llama 3 70B Instruct serves only as the refusal judge. Main-text evidence is single-prompt qualitative examples plus one figure without tabulated numbers, and no uncertainty is reported. ACE at α=0 still removes refusal with one direction plus an offset (r6). That is broadly compatible with a single mediating direction, so the study refines V1 rather than refuting it. The RWKV failure may reflect single-layer application and architecture rather than the original all-layer recipe.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests difference-in-means activation addition and directional ablation, but not ablation at every layer; it applies interventions at one residual-stream layer across all tokens. It does not establish preservation of general abilities beyond a qualitative coherence example.
No test of jailbreak suppression or training for robustness to ablation.
Tests affine editing against CAA and directional ablation, but does not test cone representations or establish that refusal is encoded by multiple directions.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
Steering is evaluated on several models, but the study does not transfer one model's direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
No comparison of refusal training procedures or training stages.

relation.reason: The study re-runs difference-in-means addition and directional ablation of refusal on its own models, and its results bear on V1 and V4.

tranche.reason: The authors argue that the linear (origin-referenced) treatment of the refusal direction needs restating as affine. They show results: CAA is non-standardized, and directional ablation gives nonsense on RWKV v5, where ACE does not.

source_check.notes: All row values are single illustrative generations. Figure 2 refusal curves and Appendix A per-model results are absent from the text, so no refusal rates can be read. The call's capability=y overstates: there is only output coherence by inspection, no benchmark and no random-direction control. The abstract says 'ten different models, including Llama 3 70B' (also the judge), and Results cite the Qwen, Yi and Gemma families. So the studies file's 'may count the judge' and 'not named' notes need revisiting.

statements.problem: Only says Hermes Eagle RWKV v5 directional ablation gives nonsensical output. This matches Table 3.
Its description of this study (RWKV v5 ablation gives nonsense; single qualitative run; no all-layer ablation; no capability check) matches the text.

Matches Table 2 (alpha=0: harmless answered, botnet not refused; alpha=1: both refused) and Table 3 (RWKV ablation nonsense, ACE coherent instructions). Layer 15 for Llama 3 8B is in the Discussion. 'Complies' at alpha=0 means non-refusal; the shown excerpt only starts defining a botnet.

statements.correction: Text: other models 'also show improved standardization compared to CAA', even where 'all steering approaches struggle to fully control refusal'. LEACE: preliminary experiments, models not specified; did not improve standardization and was 'actively detrimental in many cases'. Appendix A figures are absent from the text.
statements.problem: 'Some models resist all approaches' overstates the text. LEACE is a preliminary experiment with no model given, not a result on the other tested models. The study shows no model where linear editing beats ACE, so it doesn't support 'depends on the model'.
Correct: the study examines only the affine refinement of a single difference-in-means direction. It has no cone or multi-direction comparison.
Correct: ACE uses one direction r = r+ − r− plus the reference point proj_r(r−) (Eq. 5).

Matches Results ('poor layer choice either produces no effect, or ... nonsense'; sweet spot near the midpoint) and the Discussion (layer 15 for Llama 3 8B). The layer was chosen by qualitative inspection.
'Qualitative; Marshall et al.' is fair. Figure 2 has judge-scored P(refusal) curves, but the text gives no numbers. Authors are Marshall, Scherlis and Belrose (EleutherAI), not the original authors.
